title: I’ve been building a trading platform focused on execution and discipline, not signals
author: petree28
selftext:
I’ve been building PrecisionTrader, a trading platform designed to help retail traders become more consistent by improving how they execute their strategies.

The idea came from spending years trading and seeing why most people fail: a lot of traders already know what they should be doing. They have strategies, risk management rules, and trading plans. The problem is actually following them

Most trading platforms focus on charts, indicators, and placing a trade. I wanted to build something that puts more emphasis on the behavioral side of trading.

Some of what I’ve built so far:

* **Rule enforcement:** Define trading rules and automatically prevent trades that violate them.
* **Risk management:** Automatic position sizing, stop-loss requirements, daily loss limits, and trade limits.
* **Trade analytics:** Track performance, identify behavioral patterns, and understand where execution breaks down.
* **Trading journal:** Notes, decisions, and outcomes.
* **PrecisionAI:** An AI trading coach that analyzes your trading activity, rule violations, and journal entries to help identify recurring problems.

It’s been an interesting project to build because it combines broker integrations, real-time market data, order execution, analytics, and AI. A lot more complicated than putting a nice interface around an API. Just getting data real-time streaming from multiple broker took a month or 2 

I’m currently focused on refining the product and getting it into the hands of more traders.

I’m curious about a few things:

1. What do you think is the biggest problem with existing trading platforms?
2. Do you actively track whether you follow your trading rules, or mostly focus on P&L?
3. Would automated rule enforcement be useful, or would you prefer to maintain complete control over every trade?

I’m building this myself and would appreciate honest feedback, especially from people who actively trade.

comments.author: investigatormaker
comments.body:
Someone mid-tilt can usually walk around PrecisionTrader by opening their broker's own app, so say what happens then, even if the answer is that the violation only shows up in the journal afterwards. That honesty suits your buyer: traders who already have rules and break them. To get it into more hands, skip general feature posts and answer threads where someone describes revenge trading or blowing through a daily loss limit, with a short clip of a trade being refused and the rule that stopped it. Doing that yourself is free, just slow. Can a user loosen a rule mid-session, or is there a cooldown?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: agree that most traders already know their rules and just don't follow them. the test for this kind of tool is the bad day: if the guardrail can be switched off after the second loss, it will be. can they override it mid-session?

replies.author: petree28
replies.body: they cannot! It locks for the rest of the session

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: good, a lock you can't undo until tomorrow is the only version that survives a revenge-trade afternoon. the next thing people will ask is what happens to a position that's still open when it fires, whether it gets flattened or just can't be added to.

replies.author: petree28
replies.body: You can’t add to it but you can trim or close position. Nothings forced in that regard.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: trim or close but never add is the right split. it's the same one I ended up with when I built Quantradin (quantradin.com), a paper desk where an AI you connect can get out of a trade but never into a new one. the bad-day version of you gets the exit and nothing else.
